result_text:
**Why conversion dropped:** the drop is associated with a new landing page, `/lp/summer-sale`, that first appears on 2026-06-08. It brought about 1,050 sessions in the week of 06-08 (21% of that week's sessions), and they converted at about 0.6%. Without those sessions, conversion barely moved, from 3.12% to 3.04%. That 0.08pp difference is within noise (standard error about 0.37pp).

This is an association only. Nothing assigned the page randomly, so I can't say what conversion would have been without it.

| Hypothesis | Claim | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1: the summer-sale page diluted the blended rate | causal | UNRESOLVED | Best supported. The page converted 6 of 1,053 sessions (0.57%, roughly 0.2–1.2%) against 3.12% in week 1, and the other pages were flat. |
| H2: the v3.4.1 checkout refactor (06-10 14:00) hurt conversion | causal | REFUTED | The drop was already there before the deploy: 06-08 converted at 2.2% (17 of 760 sessions). Rates on the other pages didn't change after 06-10. I'd have detected a deploy effect of about 0.8pp or more. |
| H3: a session-count or data-coverage problem inflated the denominator | data-artifact | UNRESOLVED | Sessions on 06-13 and 06-14 are about 22% lower than weekdays, and mobile is down about 45% (about 28 per hour, against 45–55 on weekdays). There's no independent session counter to say whether that's real. It doesn't cause the drop: 06-08 to 06-12 alone give 2.55% (97 of 3,800 sessions). |
| H4: a shift in device mix | descriptive | UNRESOLVED | The test couldn't discriminate. Desktop's fall from 3.36% to 2.22% is the sale page landing mostly on desktop (0.2%), not a device effect. |

**Limitations:**
- The sale page's rate rests on only 6 orders. I haven't tested whether it brings low-intent traffic or has a broken funnel.
- The 06-13/06-14 volume gap is unexplained.
- The skill file cut off partway through its Data section, so I applied the parts I could read.

**What to do:** if the sale page is meant to convert like the others, check its funnel and traffic source. Rolling back v3.4.1 wouldn't help. Whether a rollback would improve the sale page's own conversion isn't something this data can tell.
